mcqs.learning_point: Relate ionic size to lattice properties
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the effect of ionic size on lattice energy for NaCl and CsI?

options.A: NaCl has a higher lattice energy than CsI because its constituent ions are smaller.
options.B: NaCl has a lower lattice energy than CsI because its constituent ions are smaller.
options.C: Both NaCl and CsI have the same lattice energy because lattice energy does not depend on ionic size.
options.D: CsI has a higher lattice energy than NaCl because larger ions attract more strongly.

mcqs.answer: NaCl has a higher lattice energy than CsI because its constituent ions are smaller.
mcqs.explanation: Lattice energy increases when the ions involved are smaller because the distance between the oppositely charged ions is reduced, leading to stronger electrostatic attraction. Na+ and Cl- are smaller than Cs+ and I-, so NaCl exhibits a higher lattice energy than CsI. Options B, C, and D contradict this well‑established trend.

mcqs.question: All of the following are typical properties of ionic compounds EXCEPT:

options.B: Electrical conductivity in the molten or aqueous state
options.C: Brittle solid crystals that fracture on applying stress
options.D: High electrical conductivity in the solid state

mcqs.answer: High electrical conductivity in the solid state
mcqs.explanation: Ionic solids are composed of fixed ions; they do not allow free movement of charge, so they are poor conductors in the solid state. Conductivity appears only when the lattice is melted or dissolved in water (Option B). Options A, B, and C correctly describe ionic compounds, making D the exception.

mcqs.learning_point: Explain formation of cations and anions
mcqs.question: How does a neutral sodium atom become a Na⁺ cation?

options.D: By sharing one electron with a chlorine atom

mcqs.explanation: Sodium has one electron in its outermost 3s orbital. To achieve the stable noble‑gas configuration of neon, it loses that electron, forming a Na⁺ cation. Gaining electrons would produce an anion, not a cation, and sharing electrons leads to covalent bonding, not ionic cation formation.

mcqs.question: Which description best represents the formation of an ionic bond between magnesium and chlorine?

options.A: Magnesium shares two electrons equally with two chlorine atoms.
options.B: Magnesium transfers two electrons to two chlorine atoms, producing Mg²⁺ and 2Cl⁻ which attract each other.
options.C: Magnesium and chlorine form a metallic lattice with delocalised electrons.
options.D: Magnesium accepts two electrons from chlorine atoms to become Mg²⁻.

mcqs.answer: Magnesium transfers two electrons to two chlorine atoms, producing Mg²⁺ and 2Cl⁻ which attract each other.
mcqs.explanation: In ionic bonding, the metal (Mg) loses electrons to achieve a stable configuration, forming a cation (Mg²⁺). Each chlorine atom gains one electron, becoming Cl⁻. The electrostatic attraction between Mg²⁺ and the two Cl⁻ ions constitutes the ionic bond. Option A describes covalent sharing, C describes metallic bonding, and D reverses the electron flow.

mcqs.question: Lattice energy is best defined as:

options.A: The energy required to break one mole of an ionic solid into its constituent gaseous ions.
options.B: The energy released when one mole of gaseous ions combine to form an ionic solid.
options.C: The enthalpy change when an element is converted from its standard state to gaseous atoms.
options.D: The heat absorbed when a solid ionic compound melts.

mcqs.answer: The energy released when one mole of gaseous ions combine to form an ionic solid.
mcqs.explanation: Lattice energy (U) is the exothermic energy change accompanying the formation of one mole of an ionic lattice from its gaseous ions. Option A describes the lattice dissociation energy (the reverse process). Options C and D refer to unrelated thermodynamic quantities.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate ionic size to lattice properties
mcqs.question: If the ionic radius of the cation in a crystal lattice is increased while the anion size remains unchanged, what is the expected effect on the lattice energy?

options.A: Lattice energy will increase because larger ions have stronger attractions.
options.B: Lattice energy will decrease because the inter‑ionic distance becomes larger.
options.C: Lattice energy will remain unchanged because only charge matters.
options.D: Lattice energy will become negative, indicating an endothermic process.

mcqs.answer: Lattice energy will decrease because the inter‑ionic distance becomes larger.
mcqs.explanation: Lattice energy is inversely proportional to the distance between the centers of the oppositely charged ions (U ∝ 1/r). Increasing the cation radius enlarges this distance, weakening electrostatic attraction and thus lowering lattice energy. Option A is opposite to the principle, C ignores size, and D misinterprets the sign convention.

mcqs.question: Which of the following examples best illustrates the high melting point characteristic of ionic compounds?
mcqs.explanation: NaCl is an ionic solid with strong electrostatic forces between Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions, resulting in a high melting point (~801 °C). The other substances are molecular compounds held together by weaker intermolecular forces, giving them much lower melting points.

mcqs.learning_point: Explain formation of cations and anions
mcqs.question: A metal M forms a M²⁺ ion and a non‑metal X forms an X⁻ ion. Which formula most likely represents a stable ionic compound formed from these ions?
mcqs.explanation: Charge neutrality requires the total positive charge to equal the total negative charge. One M²⁺ ion (+2) balances two X⁻ ions (2 × –1 = –2), giving the formula MX₂. Options A and B give net charges of +1 and –2 respectively, while D gives a net charge of +4, all of which are unstable.
